_comment: MEADOWS-VISUAL-PASS round 5. Runtime-only terrain shader values for the Meadows ground, merged over terrain_playground.json's `shader` block by playground_world.gd::_apply_ground_shader. Separate because terrain_playground.json fingerprints the terrain and scatter bakes, and none of this moves a vertex or a placement.

shader._comment_macro: The macro variation colours multiply the whole ground. At #b8b58c/#8ea369 they darkened and yellowed it into large olive and mustard blotches: measured on the survey's ground band at saturation 0.86-0.95 and value 0.34-0.45, against 0.52-0.66 and 0.49-0.60 across the Palworld references. Taking them most of the way to white (a render A/B through tools/survey.gd at 01, 02 and 04) brought the ground to saturation 0.62-0.70 and value 0.60-0.64 and kept a soft large-scale variation. TUNABLE. A second pass took a little red out of both (#dde3c8/#cfdfc6): at the first values the lit meadow rendered a yellow-lime (hue 62) and the paths orange. A third pass cooled both again (#d9e4cb/#cadec8): a blind round still read the ground as a yellow-olive cast against the key art's cooler greens.
shader._comment_aerial: The terrain's own distance fade (terrain_ground.gdshader) desaturated the far plain by 0.55 on top of the fog, which read as a white wall from the overlook. Halved, so distance stays green under the haze. TUNABLE.
shader._comment_blend: terrain_ground.gdshader raises each control texel's weight to the power 8 + 56 * blend_sharpness; at terrain_playground.json's 0.5 that is 36, so every 2m texel boundary between two surfaces rendered as a hard polygon edge -- a blind round read the grass on The Rise's rocky crown as 'yellow-grass islands with hard polygonal edges, like camouflage'. 0.12 (exponent about 15) keeps the height-aware blend but feathers the boundary. TUNABLE.
shader._comment_steep_rock: Expose the installed rock material on steep rendered faces, including road-painted cuts. Runtime material only: no height, collision, control paint or bake changes. Ordinary ground above normal.y 0.55 retains its authored material.

path._why_r2: r2: the tint alone barely moved the frame (the orange is in dirt_path_Color itself), so r2 swaps the albedo for a derived trodden-earth copy (saturation x0.38, value x0.86, local contrast lifted so pebbles and ruts read; tools: PIL, same 1024 size for the Terrain3D array) with a near-white tint. Every path in Meadows takes it.
path._why_r2_cpu: r2 CPU judged (26 Oct; three fresh code-blind judges, JUDGE_PROMPT verbatim, 3 anchor pairs incl. craft, confirming batch; calibrate.py linear slope 1.90, r 0.97, RMSE 0.20; Low/Compatibility llvmpipe, day approach/gameplay/detail; ralph/reports/MEADOWS/close-1024/vilpath1026-mapped.json): village_road 5.95 -> 6.97, farm_to_hall 5.95 -> 6.97, hall_front 5.76 -> 6.65; orange-smear defect PRESENT -> FIXED 9/9. Open: a single-scale blob repeat, no ruts, stones or broken grass verge. CPU no longer closes a row: OFF until the GPU pass.
path._scope: F38 village_road / band3_the_river_lock_1 close-out candidate (OFF until judged): the shipped path tint #d0b090 over dirt_path_Color reads as a flat orange road filling the village_road foreground (GPU 7.09 Medium / 6.73 High, P2-005 PARTIAL). A neutral trodden-earth tint lets the texture's own pebbles and wear read. Presentation only, no bake change.

texture_candidates._comment: Presentation-only terrain surface swaps, keyed by terrain_playground.json texture name. Kept out of terrain_playground.json because that file fingerprints the terrain and scatter bakes (a flag flip there invalidates the vegetation bake). Each applies only with its own enabled.

grass_v2._scope: F04#6 r27 / F38 (OFF): painted grass v2 (--flat) keeps blade strokes but drops the repeating dark blobs that read as smear at 1-5 m.
grass_v2._why_on: grass_v2 and soil ON (CPU-provisional improvement, not a closure): F04#6 r29 mapped 6.38 Bar A vs shipping 5.91 with three code-blind judges on the fixed F04-6 camera set (Low/Compatibility, llvmpipe; ralph/reports/LOOK/close-1022/F04-6.md). Parked by the gain rule; a GPU pass decides, and a GPU score below the bar reopens it.

soil._scope: F04#6 r27 / F38 (OFF): painted dry verge grass (--flat), the soil surface at Vance and Field.

shader_candidate._scope: F04#6 r26 / F38 candidate (OFF until judged): every yardstick judge names the Meadows ground as smeared and blurry. The macro variation multiplies the ground by about 0.8-0.85 in soft noise blobs (the camouflage smear); lighter macro, a sharper terrain mip bias and stronger near-camera grain give the ground crisp texture instead.
